text: Abel Roos. Twenty-one kyu, and I came across on the ferry this morning for this.
I have never played anybody I did not already know. So this is all quite a lot.
You don't play at all. Right.
Then no, and it isn't you. I have played four people in my life and I knew all four of them, and starting with somebody who doesn't know how the stones come off is not how I get to five.
There's a woman at the bar down the steps who teaches. Wren. Go and be taught, and then come back and I'll be nervous at you properly.
Would you -- sorry. Would you want a game?
It doesn't have to count. Nothing in here counts. That's rather the appeal of it.

exit.intro: He puts the bowls out the wrong way round, swaps them, and then swaps them back.

text: Right. Yes. I'll be here -- I've another forty minutes on this machine and nowhere in this city to be.
You beat me. That's fine. That's what I came for, people who'd beat me.
Sorry. That came out sounding as though I'd planned it.
I won. I genuinely do not know what to do with my face.
Would you play another? I'd like to find out whether that was me or whether that was you having a bad one.
